marta: heads up — found a weird auth bug in the Python SDK AsyncClient when mixing env var API_KEY and explicit api_key param :thinking_face:

marta: repro below, pretty small:
```py
# set REDWOOD_API_KEY=env_key
from redwood import AsyncClient

# trying to create a client with a different key
client = AsyncClient(api_key="explicit_key")
await client.generate(... )  # ends up using env_key instead of explicit_key
```

marta: logs show: `auth: using api key from env` even though I passed one. Happens in our async worker where multiple clients are created for different tenants.

eli: :eyes: can you paste stack trace / sdk version?

marta: SDK 0.8.4 (pip). stack looks like this: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 72, in handle_request
    await client.generate(...)
  File "/.../site-packages/redwood/client/async_client.py", line 140, in generate
    headers = await self._auth.get_headers()
  File "/.../site-packages/redwood/auth.py", line 56, in get_headers
    key = os.getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY") or self._configured_key
AttributeError: 'AsyncLocalAuth' object has no attribute '_configured_key'
```

marta: I hacked the auth.py and saw there's module-level cache/read of env var at import time and the async auth wrapper doesn't set configured_key correctly when client passed api_key. Seems racey when multiple clients are created in different tasks.

samir: ugh that sounds like the old global-default issue. Are you instantiating clients in different event loops or reusing a global session?

marta: we create per-tenant clients inside request handlers (so same loop). repro in a pytest async test: spawn 4 tasks creating clients with different keys, some tasks pick up others' keys.

eli: also related — I noticed AsyncClient.__init__ type hints currently accept api_key: str | None. If we want rotation support it'd be nice to accept a callable or async callable provider: Union[str, Callable[[], str], Callable[[], Awaitable[str]]]. Right now mypy flags when I try to pass a lambda that fetches from the vault.

samir: good call. two separate problems: (1) bug where env var fallback is evaluated incorrectly / relying on import-time state, (2) ergonomics for rotating keys. For (1) quick fix: stop reading env var at module import; read on auth.get_headers() and prefer explicit configured key when provided. Also ensure AsyncLocalAuth stores configured_key always. I'll open a PR.

marta: would you also accept a patch to make api_key param accept a callable? I can prototype.

samir: yes please. impl details: allow api_key to be Union[str, Callable[[], str], Callable[[], Awaitable[str]]]. Internally, wrap into an async provider function. Keep old behavior if str provided. Add tests for sync/async providers and concurrency.

eli: small gotcha for typing: update stub so api_key: str | Callable[..., Any] is narrowed properly. For public typing we should export a Protocol maybe: class APIKeyProvider(Protocol): async def __call__(self) -> str: ... and allow sync wrappers. That keeps mypy happy.

marta: for key rotation semantics, we also need an invalidation API on the client so cached auth tokens (if any) can be refreshed between requests. otherwise provider is called every request which may be fine but we want caching with TTL.

samir: agree — plan: provider used to fetch raw secret (api key) and Auth layer can optionally wrap with cached token logic. Default: call provider each time (consistent), optional param token_cache_ttl or a caching decorator util. I'll include a small caching util in auth.

devex-bot: Created ticket RED-5123: "async client env var override + api_key provider support" and linked branch.

marta: thanks. can we get a patch that doesn't break sync client behavior? we have older code that assumes env var is global.

samir: will keep sync parity. fix will be backwards compatible: if api_key not provided and env var present, behave same; but make sure env var is read lazily and per-instance. add unit tests to cover multiple clients in concurrent tasks.

eli: also add docs snippet for passing a callable (vault fetch example) and a short example of rotation with cached TTL.

marta: rough timeline? we hit this in staging and it's blocking a tenant rollout (keys rotate frequently).

samir: I'll draft PR today, tests tomorrow. if QA good we can ship patch release 0.8.5. deploy-bot: can you queue a canary once the release is cut?

deploy-bot: Canary job queued for channel staging-canary, job id canary-7812 :rocket:

marta: awesome, thanks all. I'll attach failing test to the ticket. :pray:

samir: thanks — will ping here when PR is up and request reviews.

eli: moving to follow-up: add typing docs and a migration note for users relying on module-level env read.

marta: noted, will update the internal onboarding sample that shows per-tenant client creation.

marta: tl;dr — bug: AsyncClient can pick up wrong key when env var and explicit api_key used concurrently. fix: lazy env read, accept callable providers, add caching options.
